samples.summary: `ciRunsFor` truncates the run path at the first `@`, so a workflow file literally named `ci.yml@<anything>.yml` still matches CI — re-opening the forgery this change exists to close
samples.evidence: `ciRunsFor` matches with `String(r?.path ?? "").split("@")[0] === CI_WORKFLOW_PATH` (checks.mjs:62). GitHub picks up ANY `*.yml`/`*.yaml` file at the top of `.github/workflows/`, and `@` is a legal git/POSIX filename character. An actor who can push a branch to the base repo (the exact adversary CI_WORKFLOW_PATH's comment names — `agent:managed` human PRs are explicitly not restricted, checks.mjs:49-52) adds `.github/workflows/ci.yml@x.yml` with `on: push` and a job that exits 0. Its run reports `path: .github/workflows/ci.yml@x.yml`, `ciRunsFor` strips at the `@`, `ciConclusion` (newest id wins — the forged run is created after the real one) returns "success", and `mark-ready.mjs:138` gate 1 — the gate whose header calls itself UNFORGEABLE — reads green with no real CI. `set-state.mjs:228` is fooled the same way. Note the three workflow `if:` gates added in this diff use EXACT equality (`path == '.github/workflows/ci.yml'`), so the reader is strictly more permissive than the triggers it is supposed to mirror. The `@ref` tolerance also buys nothing it claims to: a called/reusable workflow reports `owner/repo/.github/workflows/x.yml@ref`, which never equals the bare path after the split anyway. Fix: compare the path exactly, as the workflow gates do.

samples.summary: Matching CI by workflow path does not make gate 1 unforgeable: a `pull_request` CI run executes the PR branch's OWN `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, so gutting that file yields a genuinely green run at the exact path
samples.evidence: mark-ready.mjs:7-12 and checks.mjs:41-58 both justify the new filter with "only one file can occupy `.github/workflows/ci.yml`". That is true of the path but not of its CONTENTS on a PR branch: for `pull_request` events GitHub runs the workflow definition from the PR's merge ref, i.e. the branch's copy of ci.yml. An `agent:managed` same-repo PR (or any contributor with push access — the adversary the comment names) can therefore edit `.github/workflows/ci.yml` to make `verify-self`/`verify-browser`/`verify-integration` no-ops, get a real `success` run whose `path` is exactly `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, and satisfy both gate 1 (mark-ready.mjs:138) and the promote job's `needs.ci.outputs.conclusion == 'success'` (agent-review-panel.yml:1464) with no tests having run. CODEOWNERS `/.github/workflows/` (.github/CODEOWNERS:53) only gates the MERGE, not the draft→ready promotion this gate controls. The hardening is still an improvement over name matching, but the "UNFORGEABLE" claim in the header and in docs/design/harness-engineering.md is not established; closing it needs something the PR cannot rewrite (e.g. requiring the run's `head_branch`/definition to come from the base ref, or checking the required check-run contexts by name rather than the workflow conclusion).

samples.summary: The "exactly one CI run per PR head SHA" invariant that newest-wins rests on is not actually guaranteed by the trigger set the new tripwire test pins
samples.evidence: `ciConclusion`'s contract (checks.mjs:69-75) and the new test `ci.yml's triggers keep exactly one CI run per PR head SHA` (checks.test.mjs) assert that only `push`(main)/`merge_group`/`pull_request` exist, therefore one run per head SHA. `pull_request` uses GitHub's default activity types (ci.yml:9-10 declares no `types:`), which include `reopened` — closing and reopening a PR files a SECOND `pull_request` CI run for the same head SHA, as does opening a second PR from the same commit. The tripwire test cannot see either, so it certifies an invariant the triggers do not enforce. Newest-wins still reads the current run in those cases, so this is assurance quality rather than a live bypass — but any future reasoning that leans on "there is only ever one run" (as this diff's comments and the design doc do) is leaning on something untrue.

samples.summary: Gate 1 reads a single unpaginated page of workflow runs for the head SHA, so a run-flood can push the CI run off the page
samples.evidence: `ciPassed` calls `actions/runs?head_sha=${sha}&per_page=100` (mark-ready.mjs:131) and never paginates, while the re-run mirrors in this same diff switched to `github.paginate`. A branch carrying >100 workflow files (or a heavily-instrumented repo) produces more than 100 runs for one head SHA; whichever runs fall off the page are invisible to `ciRunsFor`. With GitHub's newest-first ordering this fails closed (gate reads "CI has not run", PR stays a draft), so the impact is denial of promotion rather than a bypass — but the gate's correctness now depends on an undocumented API ordering guarantee. Same pattern at set-state.mjs:225.

samples.summary: The gate's own security header now misdescribes what it enforces: it says EVERY ci.yml run must be green, while the code reads only the newest
samples.evidence: mark-ready.mjs:7-8 was rewritten by this diff to read "EVERY run of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` for the PR head SHA concluded `success`", but `ciPassed` delegates to `ciConclusion` (mark-ready.mjs:138), which by design takes the newest run only (checks.mjs:90-94) — the every-run rule was explicitly reverted in this same change. The header of an "unforgeable" gate is the document a future reviewer trusts when deciding whether a second run for the SHA is a hole; stating a stricter rule than the code implements invites exactly the wrong conclusion.

samples.summary: The crash-vs-verdict discriminator greps the whole captured log, which also contains `gh` stderr echoed through error messages
samples.evidence: The `1)` branch decides "gates said no" vs "node crashed" with `grep -qF "Not promoting: one or more gates are not satisfied" "$RUNNER_TEMP/mark-ready.log"` (agent-review-panel.yml:1539). The log is stdout AND stderr (`2>&1`, line 1509), and mark-ready echoes `execFileSync` error messages that carry `gh`'s own stderr (e.g. mark-ready.mjs:113). Any path that reproduces that sentence in the log turns a crash into the benign "gates-unsatisfied" outcome. The direction is fail-safe (the PR stays a draft either way, no promotion), so this is hardening only — matching on the last line, or on a dedicated machine-readable marker, would remove the ambiguity.

verdict.reason: The described code exists verbatim: checks.mjs:62 truncates the run path at the first `@` before comparing to CI_WORKFLOW_PATH (checks.mjs:58), which destroys the uniqueness property the docstring (checks.mjs:53-56, "only one file can occupy it") relies on to call gate 1 unforgeable. Any workflow file named `.github/workflows/ci.yml@<anything>.yml` produces a run whose reported path collapses to the CI path. Both consumers are reachable and unguarded: mark-ready.mjs:131 fetches runs for the head SHA with no workflow_id scoping and mark-ready.mjs:138 passes the raw list to ciConclusion; set-state.mjs:226-228 does the same. ciConclusion takes newest-by-id (checks.mjs:90-99), so a forged run created after the real one wins. The threat actor is explicitly in the design's own model and explicitly unrestricted (checks.mjs:49-52, agent:managed human PRs). The workflow-side gates use exact equality (agent-iterate-ci.yml:54, ci-report.yml:56, agent-review-panel.yml:117,166), confirming the JS reader is more permissive than the triggers it mirrors. No guard, no filtering call site, and no test covers the prefix collision (checks.test.mjs:193,498,519 only cover a wholly distinct path and the @ref suffix). In-lane as an access-control/integrity bypass of the promote gate.

verdict.reason: The cited code exists exactly as described. checks.mjs:58-63 identifies CI solely by `path === ".github/workflows/ci.yml"`, and mark-ready.mjs:127-141 treats that run's `success` conclusion as unforgeable evidence (header claim at mark-ready.mjs:4-12). But ci.yml:6-10 triggers on `pull_request`, and a `pull_request` run executes the PR branch's OWN copy of ci.yml — so a same-repo branch that no-ops verify-self/verify-browser/verify-integration produces a genuinely green run at precisely that path, satisfying gate 1 and the promote job's `needs.ci.outputs.conclusion == 'success'` (agent-review-panel.yml:1464) with no tests run. The path filter defeats a *second* file claiming `name: CI`; it does not defeat rewriting the file at that path. No guard closes it: the panel gate (agent-review-panel.yml:164-169) excludes forks but deliberately admits same-repo `agent:managed` human PRs, and the workflow's own comment (lines 50-52) plus checks.mjs:49-52 name that same actor as the unrestricted adversary; CODEOWNERS gates merge, not the draft→ready flip. Impact is bounded (the ready flag carries no merge authority, per harness-engineering.md:2182-2184), which supports `major` rather than `critical`, but a weakened/bypassable authorization gate that reads as covered is squarely in the security lane. No refutation ground applies.
